artists.biography:
Steven John Wilson (born 3 November 1967) is an English musician, best known as the founder, lead guitarist, singer and songwriter of progressive rock band Porcupine Tree. He is involved in many other bands and musical projects both as musician and producer (including No-Man and Blackfield) and also maintains a solo career.
Wilson is a self-taught producer, audio engineer, guitar and keyboard player, playing other instruments as and where required (including bass guitar, concert harp, hammered dulcimer and flute).
He used to split his living time between Tel Aviv and London, England, but he no longer holds a permanent residence in Tel Aviv.

For me the golden period for music was the late sixties and early seventies, when the album became the primary means of artistic expression, when musicians liberated themselves from the 3 minute pop song format, and started to draw on jazz and classical music especially, combining it with the spirit of psychedelia to create “journeys in sound” I guess you could call them. So without being retro, my album is a kind of homage to that spirit. There’s everything from Morricone-esque film themes to choral music to piano ballads to a 23 minute progressive jazz –inspired piece. perplexity.description:
Grace for Drowning is Steven Wilson's second solo studio album, released by Kscope on September 26, 2011, as a double album. It marked Wilson's first major solo work following Porcupine Tree's dissolution in 2010, establishing his trajectory as a solo artist after the band's breakup. The album represents a deliberate artistic expansion, with Wilson describing it as more experimental and eclectic than his previous solo effort, Insurgentes. Drawing inspiration from the progressive rock era of the late 1960s and early 1970s, the album embraces the extended compositional formats and genre-blending approaches characteristic of that period, incorporating elements of jazz, classical music, and psychedelia into its progressive rock framework.

Musically, Grace for Drowning demonstrates Wilson's ambition to create what he termed "journeys in sound"—extended pieces that liberate themselves from conventional pop song structures. The double album format allows for this expansive vision, showcasing the crossover progressive rock style that defines much of his solo work. The album's production reflects Wilson's meticulous approach to sound design, with longtime collaborator Lasse Hoile providing the album artwork photography.

The album achieved significant recognition within the progressive rock community and received a Grammy nomination for Best Surround Sound Album at the 54th Annual Grammy Awards, reflecting both its technical ambition and artistic merit. This accolade underscored Wilson's standing as a serious artist in the progressive rock landscape during the early 2010s.
